digest.component_or_area: MCP error surface and shared error classification
propositions: MCP tool failures currently lack the structured `error` discriminator that the CLI emits via `error_envelope`, forcing agents to pattern-match unstructured exception prose to distinguish failure types.

A central error code classifier does not exist; codes are scattered as bare string literals across 12 CLI call sites and two ad-hoc shapes in MCP, making it impossible to verify that all three interfaces (library, CLI, MCP) emit identical codes for the same failure.

The library interface exposes no machine `error` discriminator; `error_code_for(exc)->str` must be added to `src/rebar/_errors.py` so a three-way cross-interface test can assert agreement without inspection.
MCP failures must carry `error_envelope` (with `error`, `message`, and optional `input`) delivered via `McpEnvelopeError` on the `ToolError.__cause__`, with envelope JSON in the wire `isError` text.

Two existing MCP soft-error returns (`_mcp_reads.py` explain_criterion and `_mcp_llm.py`) use divergent ad-hoc shapes and must be migrated to carry a vocabulary `error` code while preserving agent-branching fields (`kind`, `resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic`).

The `error_envelope` schema currently requires `input`, but MCP failures not tied to a target (e.g., gate refusals) have no input to resolve; `input` must be moved from required to optional while keeping CLI output byte-identical.
